title: Holistic prefetch admission and cache sanity pass for continuous batch runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 12 months we've added multiple prefetch and admission heuristics to the continuous batching pipeline to improve token-utilization and reduce per-token cost. Those changes were tactical and introduced a few Rust/Go boundaries in the hot path, subtle cache consistency windows, and duplicate admission paths that occasionally cause small tail-latency spikes and KV-store read amplification.

Goal: Perform a focused "sanity pass" to (1) harmonize the prefetch/admission code paths so a single admission flow decides prefetch vs immediate dispatch, (2) tighten KV cache consistency windows and add explicit reconciliation hooks, and (3) trim scheduler handoff cruft that adds contention under high multiplexing. This is a tech-debt cleanup with measurable perf/operational outcomes.

Non-goals: This is NOT a full rewrite of the batcher or scheduler. We are not changing the batching contract or introducing new hardware/kernel selection logic. Larger scope items will be tracked separately.

Scope and work items:
- Audit existing prefetch/admission code (hot path) and collapse duplicate decision trees into a single AdmissionController module behind feature flag runtime.prefetch_v2.
- Replace ad-hoc KV-cache "soft-stale" window with an explicit versioned validity interval and a fast-path reconciliation that runs in the background when leases are reclaimed.
- Remove one synchronous RPC in the scheduler handoff path that serializes slot allocation under burst load; replace with probabilistic backoff + lease hinting.
- Add tracing spans and metric labels to cover: admission.decision, kv.cache_hit_reason, kv.reconcile_duration, scheduler.handoff_latency.
- Add e2e microbench harness that replays recorded real traffic (short/long sequences) and validates token-per-second and tail latency delta.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met):
1) End-to-end tail (p95/p99) latency for mixed short+long sequences does not regress; target p99 <= baseline + 3%.
2) Token throughput improves or remains equal for steady-state bursts; target >= baseline tokens/sec - 0%.
3) KV read amplification reduced by >= 18% in benchmarked traces (replay harness).
4) No increase in error surface (no new 5xx paths) and all critical traces have proper trace/span annotations.
5) Feature-gated rollout path exists with canary on 5% traffic, observability dashboards for new metrics, and automatic rollback on error rate spike.

Rollout plan: merge under feature flag runtime.prefetch_v2 -> internal canary (staging) -> canary 5% prod with manual watch -> gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if metrics stable.

Notes on trade-offs: collapsing admission paths simplifies reasoning and will likely reduce hot-path branching, but may require a small additional allocation in the common case (compensated by KV-hit improvements). Probabilistic backoff in the scheduler reduces serialization but may slightly increase mean wait on extreme saturation; we accept that for lower tail variance.

Related artifacts: design doc (internal), perf csvs, PR for the first patch. See attachments and comments for links.
comments: 2025-11-03 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket after perf review session. Observed read amplification around KVLease expiry; proposed single AdmissionController consolidating existing heuristics.

2025-11-05 — Jonah Meyer: Spike completed (branch runtime/prefetch-sanity). Found three admission code paths across layers: frontend, batcher, and scheduler. Candidate consolidation points mapped in repo. Small benchmark showing 12% lower kv reads in replay when we short-circuit duplicate lookups.

2025-11-07 — Claire Nguyen (Design): Reviewed plan; asked that we keep existing telemetry labels for client attribution and add a concise diagram for decision flow in confluence. Linked design sketch: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RT/pages/holistic-prefetch-schematic

2025-11-10 — Jonah Meyer: Implemented initial AdmissionController + feature flag toggle. Added unit tests for versioned validity interval on kvcache. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423 (WIP).

2025-11-12 — Eng QA (Marco Ruiz): Ran replay harness against PR branch; observed 21% drop in duplicate reads and p99 improved by ~1.6% on medium bursts. Noted two intermittent failing traces where lease reconciliation raced with eviction. Added reconciliation backoff and a mutex-free hint path.

2025-11-16 — Jonah Meyer: Removed a synchronous scheduler RPC and replaced with lease hint + exponential jitter. Microbench shows reduced lock contention under multiplexing (cpu sys% down 8%). Added new metrics: kv.reconcile_duration and scheduler.handoff_latency.

2025-11-18 — PM review (Elena Torres): Reviewed acceptance criteria and asked for explicit rollback condition: if error-rate delta > 0.5% or p99 increase > 5% in canary, rollback immediately. Updated rollout steps.

2025-11-20 — Jonah Meyer: Merged final changes behind runtime.prefetch_v2 flag. Canary will start 2025-11-21. Observability dashboards prepared. Next: monitor canary and follow rollback/runbook if needed.
